$note: LAYER 2. Roles, not values. Every colour role is MODE-PAIRED in a single map: { dark, light }. This is the structural fix for the drift bug — the old system kept two parallel maps (text/lText in tokens.ts, and a separate @theme block), which is exactly the shape that let lTextMut and safety exist in one place and not the other. With pairing, a missing light value is a schema failure at build time rather than a comment nobody read.
$provenance: dark = Figma (canonical for colour). light = code (Figma has no light-mode frames).

card.$description: Surface nested inside a raised one. Light mode collapses this onto white — the light palette separates by border, dark by fill.

notification.$description: A surface that stays DARK IN BOTH MODES on purpose. Exists for the transient confirmation pill, which follows the platform snackbar convention: a dark pill reads as system chrome rather than as part of the page, and on a light screen that is exactly what makes a two-second message noticeable without shouting. Mode-invariant is the whole point — do not 'fix' it by pairing it, and do not reach for it as a general surface.

secondary.$description: Labels, captions, supporting copy, and locked-row labels.

muted.$description: Placeholders and fine print. NOW AA-SAFE in both modes (4.52–5.45 dark, 4.54–4.84 light). NOTE the consequence: a muted step that meets AA necessarily sits close to the secondary step, so the three-tier text hierarchy compresses toward two. Differentiate quiet text by WEIGHT and SIZE, not by lowering contrast — which is the accessible way to build hierarchy regardless.

onAccent.$description: Label on a filled accent surface. Mode-invariant because the accent fill is.

onNotification.$description: Label on surface.notification. Mode-invariant for the same reason: the surface it sits on is.

default.$description: Brand accent for NON-TEXT use: active tab, progress fill, selected outline, focus ring. Mode-invariant by design.

strong.$description: Accent-coloured TEXT: links, unlock pills, accumulation counters. 5.82:1 dark, 4.55:1 light. Light uses a dedicated darker step because the brand accent reaches only 4.19:1 there.

dim.$description: Deep accent tint for gradient starts and tinted card fills.

surface.$description: An accent-tinted CONTAINER: informational cards, badges, chips, callouts. This NAMES a value the system already used five times without a general name — corridor.phaseChip, accumulation.counterFill, historyFade.pillFill, report.changeBlock and state.selectedFill are all accent at 13%. Those names each claim a specific meaning, so reusing one for a plain informational card would have been misnaming rather than reuse. Nothing new was chosen here; the value was promoted to the name it had earned.

edge.$description: The border that goes with accent.surface. Same 27% step as state.selectedEdge, and decorative for the same reason: the tinted fill carries the grouping, so the border is reinforcement rather than the sole affordance.

category.$note:
MARK vs INK vs ON-MARK. This is the most important distinction in this system, and it has three members rather than two because a fill needs a foreground.

`mark` — DECORATIVE FILLS ONLY: chip backgrounds, icon tiles, chart bands, dots. Exempt from contrast because it never carries meaning alone; a chip always has a label and an icon tile always has a glyph.

`ink` — anything that CONVEYS meaning: text, icons, and data strokes such as chart lines. Must meet contrast. On dark the pastels already clear 7.7–12.4:1 so ink reuses them; on light they reach only 1.47–1.96:1, so ink switches to dedicated darkened values.

`onMark` — the foreground for text placed ON a mark fill. MODE-INVARIANT, because the mark it sits on is: a pastel does not change between modes, so a foreground chosen for one mode is automatically right for the other. It resolves near-black rather than white, and that is the whole point — white on these pastels reaches 1.47–1.96:1 in BOTH modes, which is worse than any failure ever tracked as debt here, while near-black reaches 9.5–10.9:1.

WHY onMark HAD TO EXIST. `ink` is not a substitute: ink is calibrated to sit on the SURFACE or on a tint of the mark, not on the full-strength mark, and it is mode-paired so its dark value is the pastel itself — which on a pastel fill would be invisible. Before this token there was simply no approved answer to 'I filled something with a category colour, what colour is the label', so two call sites answered `#fff` and neither pair was ever declared.

Every family must define mark + ink + icon + label or the build fails; that is how 'never meaning by colour alone' becomes mechanical.

ink.$description: Ratios are on the primitive, calibrated against the tinted backdrops this actually sits on. Shifted toward plum so it cannot be mistaken for the reserved safety red.

onMark.$description: 9.9:1 on the pain fill, both modes.
9.5:1 on the sleep fill, both modes. Replaces the #fff on the pre-appointment View button, which was 1.81:1.

ink.$description: Ratios are on the primitive. Its mark was the worst pair in the system at 1.47:1.

onMark.$description: 11.9:1 on the energy fill, both modes.
10.9:1 on the mood fill, both modes. Replaces the #fff on the weekly card's Save to timeline button, which was 1.58:1 — the worst measured pair in the product.
9.5:1 on the medication fill, both modes.

painScale.$note:
The 0–10 pain severity scale, mark/ink split per step — the same distinction as color.category, applied to a SCALE rather than a single hue.

It is declared step-by-step rather than as one token because that is what makes it auditable: a scale audited at one value tells you nothing about the other ten, and the failure it replaced was concentrated in the MIDDLE of the range (score 3 was the worst at 1.37:1) where a single spot-check would never have looked.

`mark` fills the slider track. `ink` writes the numeral. Consume through painStep(mode, score), which clamps and rounds — the score is user input from a range input, and an out-of-range index silently returning undefined is how a colour becomes 'transparent' at run time.

cta.$note: The primary call to action carries its OWN gradient rather than reusing the brand accent. White on the brand accent reaches 4.19:1 at the dark stop and 2.84:1 at the light stop, and the label is 16px at weight 600 — body text under WCAG, so 4.5:1 applies. Rather than shift the brand hue everywhere, the CTA gets darker dedicated stops and the accent stays intact for non-text use.

to.$description: Gradient end — the worst case for the label. White 4.77:1.

safety.$note: RESERVED. These are the only tokens permitted to resolve to the alert hues, and restricted.mjs fails the build if that hue appears outside this family. Split into ink and mark for the same reason as the categories.

ink.$description: Red-flag TEXT. Mode-paired so it clears 4.5:1 on both palettes — 4.79–5.77 dark, 4.70–5.01 light. The original single hue reached 4.38 and 3.54.

mark.$description: Red-flag icons, borders and fills, where the 3:1 non-text threshold applies. Preserves the original hue.

disabled.$description: Disabled control fill. The only disabled-CTA reference in the design file is Figma node 1:96.

selectedFill.$description: Selected option-card fill. The standard 13% tint.

selectedEdge.$description: Selected option-card border. The standard 27% tint; 13 uses. DEBT: 1.40/1.38:1 against the 3:1 non-text threshold.

scrim.$description: Dimming layer behind a sheet or overlay.

type.$note: Role -> { size, weight, lineHeight, tracking }. Line heights are absolute, matching what Figma reports.

display.$description: Day-N counter, pain score. The emotional anchors.

buttonPrimary.$description: 16/600 — BODY text under WCAG, not large text. See the CTA note above.

insight.$description: The plain-language sentence above a chart. Styled as PRIMARY — the chart supports the sentence, not the reverse.

motion.$note: Named roles so components never quote a raw duration. Each pairs a duration with the curve it should use.

entrance.$description: Fade in and rise 16px. fill-mode both.

draw.$description: Progress fill and chart draw-in. First view only — never on re-render.

celebrate.$description: Confirmation check-mark. Resolves under a second.

ambient.$description: Slow breathing pulse. Ambient life only, never attention-getting.
